dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Pense: quantas vezes o número 7 cabe dentro do 9? Esse valor será sua parte inteira.
Tente subtrair o denominador (7) do numerador (9). O que sobrar será o novo numerador da parte fracionária, mantendo o mesmo denominador.
Você tem 9/7. Como 7/7 é igual a 1 inteiro, quanto sobra de 9/7 quando você retira esse 1 inteiro?
Quase lá! Se você tirar 7 de 9, sobram 2. Então você tem 1 inteiro e mais 2/7. Tente preencher m1=1, m2=2 e m3=7.

Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you." com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); botão "Convert" que abre as caixas do número misto (m1 = parte inteira, m2/m3 = fração restante; "-" quando não há); reta numérica de 0 a 2 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 7 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. dicas.texto: Which number describes the amount of time Eric actually used?
In a fraction, the numerator is written above the denominator and represents the part being measured.
Look for the number of days Eric took rather than the number of days in a week.
Use the number stated for the days Eric needed and enter it in the top box.
What whole unit is being used to describe the number of weeks?
Convert the whole unit into days so the numerator and denominator use the same unit.
One week is divided into an equal number of days. Use that number for the denominator.
Count the days that make one complete week and enter that count in the bottom box.
Compare the number of parts used with the number of parts in one whole.
A fraction is ... when its numerator is greater than its denominator.
Check whether the top number is larger than the bottom number.
Because more than one complete group of seven parts is represented, select the comparison showing a value above one.
A mixed number separates complete wholes from the fractional part that remains.
Divide the numerator by the denominator; use the quotient as the whole number and the remainder as the new numerator.
One complete group of seven can be taken from nine, and the unused parts keep the original denominator.
Enter the quotient in m1, the remainder in m2, and keep the denominator in m3.
Use the denominator to determine how many equal parts make one whole.
Locate 1 first, then count forward by sevenths using the numerator as the total number of parts.
After reaching 1, count two more equal intervals toward 2.
Place the point at the second tick after 1 on the seven-part scale.
Before submitting, check that the fraction describes days taken compared with the days in one week.
Review the numerator, denominator, mixed-number conversion, and number-line point.
Make sure the fraction fields and the marked point represent the same value.
When every component agrees, press Done to submit the fraction shown by your completed response.
